title: Formally smooth morphisms of schemes
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. $f$ is *formally smooth* if for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine schemes over $S$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (so $T'$ is affine, $T'\to S$ is given, and $T\to S$ is its restriction) and every morphism $a:T\to X$ over $S$, there exists a morphism $a':T'\to X$ over $S$ whose restriction to $T$ is $a$, i.e. $a'\circ i=a$ and $f\circ a'$ is the given morphism $T'\to S$: every solid commutative square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc} X & \xleftarrow{a} & T\\ f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow i\\ S & \longleftarrow & T' \end{array}
$$

admits a dotted arrow $T'\to X$ making both triangles commute.
